body:
Decision: The archivist is the default writer of records, not the only door. Hand-written records stay allowed and readable. Adopting them is an archivist task: normalise them to docs/adr-format.md, regenerate INDEX.md, set edges. `mem lint` reports and normalises drift instead of only rejecting it. `mem` and `mem-dream` are the archivist's tools, and it calls mem-dream itself when a write needs more than the neighbourhood of the new record. Lessons are NOT promoted into agent definitions (the-coder.md etc.). Those stay lean, and only the user edits them, by hand. A lesson that had to be learned a third time (third-time rule) signals failed retrieval, not a missing promotion. The archivist sharpens the record's `cue:` (the situation in which it helps) and checks whether a pull point is missing. mem-dream's job shifts accordingly: it consolidates by writing good cues, which prepares future recognition.
Why: Separating who (roles), what (records, agent definitions) and how (mem, mem-dream) keeps mem-dream from being a step someone has to remember to run. Promoting lessons into an agent definition is push by another name: the definition loads into every run whether the situation fits or not. It grows context and noise, like the retired autoinject. An agent should search its own memory at its boundary instead (an earlier record (id withheld)). The cue is the closest functional analogue of human recognition ('I have been in this situation before'). So the fix for a lesson that is not recalled is a better index, not a bigger prompt. Hand-written records already exist in three areas (an earlier record (id withheld)). The third-time rule comes from Troy's practice 4 (an earlier record (id withheld) in interview-notes).
Scope: docs/target_picture_plugin.md (roles, 'Who, what, how', 'Experience: cues, not promotions'), chunks 1, 2 and 5. Revised twice on 2026-10-10: 'only writer' became 'default writer', and the promotion of lessons into agent definitions was dropped at the user's objection.

Decision: Knowledge is addressed by the folder of its area: the nearest ancestor with docs/records/. A CLAUDE.md is not required (user, 2026-10-10). It helps where sessions start in the area (charter, routing), but plays no part in addressing. Neither a collection name nor a git repo is the address. ai-mem has no catch-all level and no personal area. Every record goes to the area of its topic. Cross-cutting topics get an area of their own: ~/workspace/ai-architecture for how the user works with AI, and a small environment area for machine and tooling facts. Whose knowledge it is goes into the record as `perspective:` (an earlier record (id withheld)). How areas relate is a context map, not a hierarchy of levels. Edges point at ids. References across areas are relative paths or area names, never absolute paths. `workspace`, `global` and `subagent.*` dissolve into areas.
Why: The user decided in ~/workspace/ai-architecture that collection names derived from the folder hierarchy go away, records live in the area's docs/records/, and they stay readable without the librarian (an earlier record (id withheld) there). Areas must be movable without a migration, and some areas are not git repos. The user also wants project knowledge kept out of a shared level, while cross-cutting questions belong in their own area. CLAUDE.md is optional because records-only folders (the records home, fresh areas) are never worked in, but must still be addressable.
Scope: mem CLI (`mem context` finds the area by path, and the mapping file and collection resolution go away), navigation reference, archivist (picks an area by topic), chunks 1, 2 and 5 of docs/target_picture_plugin.md. Open: how the hook finds areas once AI_MEM_WORKSPACE_ROOT is no longer needed for naming, and where exactly the environment area lives.

Decision: Records should become a good blueprint, so they may be edited and cleaned up deliberately (user, 2026-10-10). One question draws the line: does removing it lose a reason, or a step on the path to a decision? If yes, supersede: the record stays readable and is flagged. If no, it is dead weight and may be edited in place, merged or deleted. Examples of dead weight: stale pointers (file names, paths, counts), outdated status strings, duplicates, facts about code that no longer exists and on which no decision rests, poor wording. Edges give a checkable signal. An incoming derived_from means the record carries a reason. No incoming edges plus a vanished subject means it is probably dead weight. The doctor lists such candidates, the archivist decides, and mem-dream's split and merge fall under the same rule. Precondition: cleanup is only safe where git stands behind the records. The record is the current blueprint, and git is the archive underneath. Every area that is cleaned must be versioned. As of 2026-10-10: ~/workspace/ai-mem-records is a git repo. ai-mem/docs/records/ was taken out of .gitignore on 2026-10-10 and is versioned in the ai-mem repo; the user reviews the user records before pushing. ai-architecture and interview-notes are not repos. Fabrica will be versioned publicly.
Why: Strict immutability turns records into a pile of corpses that hides the blueprint. Unrestricted editing loses the why. Separating reasons, which are superseded, from dead weight, which is cleaned up, keeps both. It refines an earlier record (id withheld) (superseded entries are flagged, not hidden), which still applies to anything that carries a reason. Evidence stays immutable (an earlier record (id withheld)), except for the pseudonymisation exception for publication.
Scope: archivist and mem-dream rules, `mem doctor` (dead-weight candidates: no incoming edges and a missing subject), navigation reference, manifesto principle 'The record is tended', chunks 2, 4 and 5 of docs/target_picture_plugin.md.

Decision: Every file under docs/ and docs/reference/ is classified as one of three things:
(1) Current documentation of the new model, rewritten and kept current. Structured after Diátaxis: tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation.
(2) A source: dated evidence of how ai-mem got here, such as measurements, design sketches, plans, comparisons, retired systems and the origin story. Sources move to docs/sources/<slug>.md (raw material in docs/sources/<slug>/) with frontmatter (type, date, origin, status). Their claims are frozen. Conclusions that still hold become learnings and decisions that point to the source (Evidence: / derived_from).
(3) A duplicate, merged into its current counterpart, e.g. docs/developer-guide.md vs docs/reference/developer_guide.md.
Sources are part of the model, not an archive. The librarian may follow Evidence links when asked for proof. The archivist creates sources and derives learnings from them, but never edits a source's claims. The doctor lists sources that no learning points to. The format follows ~/workspace/interview-notes: 'what the source says' kept apart from 'our notes'. Internal sources such as measurements, session findings and our own past design docs count as much as external ones such as talks and papers. Every chunk updates the docs it touches. A dedicated chunk does the classification and rewrites the README concept-first.
Why: Much of today's documentation describes retired systems: hybrid search, reranking / confidence lifecycle, collections, the automation pipeline, ChromaDB. Yet it is the evidence behind current decisions. Deleting it loses the why. Keeping it as documentation misleads readers about the current system. As sources it keeps both: frozen evidence plus current docs. This extends an earlier record (id withheld) (evidence never changes) to ai-mem's own history. Diátaxis comes from the ai-architecture handoff (conclusion 1).
Scope: docs/, docs/reference/, README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/adr-format.md (source format), the archivist and doctor. A new docs-and-sources chunk in docs/target_picture_plugin.md, plus a 'docs touched are updated' exit in every chunk. The user stressed on 2026-10-10 that documentation and README must be adapted and extended.

Decision: ai-mem gets a doctor, similar to Claude Code's /doctor. It diagnoses whether the practice is still alive and changes nothing itself. Findings go to the setup assistant (wiring) or the archivist (records). Two parts:
- `mem doctor`: a deterministic CLI check, no LLM. It covers wiring (which teams/skills lack the handoff-protocol hook-in, are the hooks active), records (lint, dangling edges also across areas, records still under collection names, hand-written records not yet adopted), state (FOCUS.md or the last handoff older than recent commits), effect (rate of non-'none' records_consulted / record_candidates, hook flags for missing retro fields, lessons learned a third time) and migration (Chroma store without records_v1.done).
- A judgment part in the setup assistant: is this a real boundary in team X, is this really the same lesson.
Division of labour: the setup assistant enables once, hooks enforce per event, the doctor checks the whole picture on demand or periodically.
Why: Conventions do not break loudly, they fade (an earlier record (id withheld) in collection `workspace`). Hooks catch single events but not erosion over time or wiring that was never done. Facts are checked by code (cheap, reproducible), judgments by a role, mirroring an earlier record (id withheld). The plugin thereby enables the user's AI architecture (~/workspace/ai-architecture) instead of being only a store.
Scope: `mem doctor` in chunk 1 (and growing with later chunks), judgment part with the setup assistant in chunk 6. docs/target_picture_plugin.md.

Decision: The MCP server (server.py, mem_* tools) goes away. ai-mem becomes a Claude Code plugin without .mcp.json: a stdlib CLI for writes (format/path validation), reading via Read/Glob/Grep and the librarian, agents/skills/SessionStart hook as plugin parts, plus a setup assistant that builds the framework into the user's own workflows.
Why: The value has shifted from the tool to the practice (records in the repo, fixed retrieval points at transitions, judgment instead of a score). The change that worked (the librarian in the dev-team review) was conceptual and structural; no tool could have delivered it. The server costs restarts, stale code in running sessions and the mcp/chromadb dependencies; the file path needs only the stdlib.
Scope: Changes todo_plugin_packaging (planned there still with .mcp.json and a venv bootstrap). Related to todo_drop_chromadb_dependency. The ChromaDB store on disk stays untouched.

Decision: Records about the framework itself move to the area ~/workspace/fabrica/docs/records/ and are published with Fabrica. Fabrica was built with Fabrica: its own lodge book (charters, handoffs, evidence, superseded decisions, corrections) is the proof that the framework works (user, 2026-10-10: 'it would prove itself'). The line of thought is the valuable public part. Private details are not. The user reads and checks their own entries, or has them checked. Possibly all of them are useful publicly. Where a record or source touches private matters, it is generalised or pseudonymised in place, not withheld. Examples: the user becomes 'the Navigator', the acquaintance becomes 'an external installation with an auto-updating agent', absolute home paths become area-relative paths. This is a deliberate, explicit exception to 'evidence never changes' (an earlier record (id withheld)). For a public repo, protecting people outweighs the immutability of evidence, so no separate private original is kept. Each such change is noted in the record ('pseudonymised for publication, <date>'). Records stay with the topic they describe. ai-mem keeps the plugin-specific ones (MCP removal, doctor, docs and sources, adopting hand-written records, todos, the dev-team integration).
Why: A framework of practices is proven by its practice, not by its description. This narrows the decision of 2026-10-04 (commit 380df16), which kept docs/records/ out of the public ai-mem repo as the user's private decision graph: private details stay private, the reasoning becomes public. Pseudonymising protects third parties (manifesto principles 'The record is tended' and 'Wisdom, not only rules') without losing the why. Breaking a rule consciously and saying so is itself a Fabrica practice, now part of the manifesto's data hygiene principle ('The record is tended'): an explicit exception with a reason, not silent drift.
Scope: chunk 5 of docs/target_picture_plugin.md (fabrica as target area; the archivist proposes generalised versions and the user approves before publishing), ~/workspace/fabrica. Open: whether fabrica becomes its own public git repo.

Decision: The framework is called Fabrica. ai-mem keeps its name and is the memory plugin that supports Fabrica. Tasklies are one ritual of Fabrica, the way a retro or a daily is a ritual of Scrum. Other rituals include the charter at a session start, the handoff at a boundary, and the review against the records.
Why: The framework (conventions, roles, rituals, artifacts) is the substance, and the tool is replaceable (epistemology-framework.md, 'Synthesis', 2026-09-25). The name comes from the Latin fabrica ecclesiae, the institution that built and kept a cathedral across generations. That is the international form of the German Bauhütte: organisational memory, rituals and handoffs, apprentice and master learning from each other. English 'fabric' adds the image of woven knowledge. Keeping 'ai-mem' for the plugin avoids a breaking rename for installed users.
Scope: Manifest and framework specification (todo_split_manifest_and_name_framework), docs and README (chunk 5b), plugin description (chunk 6) in docs/target_picture_plugin.md. Name collisions (e.g. Benetton's research centre Fabrica) were not checked.

Decision: Hooks enforce THAT a ritual happens. Roles decide HOW. Planned hooks: SubagentStop checks that a [retro] block carries records_consulted and record_candidates. `mem lint` runs when records changed. At session end, a reminder to run /reflect when work was done. These hooks never inject record content. They only check or remind.
Why: ai-mem's main operational risk is convention fragility: orchestrator-only writes, [retro] blocks and mem_dream are kept by convention, not code (an earlier record (id withheld) in collection `workspace`, from dev_stack_assessment_2026_05). The plugin direction (archivist, handoffs, /reflect, handoff protocol) adds more convention. Judgment cannot be code-enforced, but call points can. This is not the retired push hooks: those injected content regardless of the situation, these enforce a ritual. Organisations keep the ADR ritual alive the same way, with PR templates and CI checks rather than good intentions.
Scope: plugin hooks/ (chunk 6), the [retro] contract (chunk 4), `mem lint` (chunk 1), docs/target_picture_plugin.md. Measure whether the hooks raise the rate of non-'none' records_consulted and record_candidates.

Decision: Every record can carry a `perspective:` field naming whose knowledge or experience it is: `user`, `agent`, or a role such as `the-coder` or `reviewer`. Location follows topic (area), never party. The librarian uses perspective as a lens, not a filter. It structures answers by party ('decided X because ...' / 'the coder experienced ...'). A contradiction between perspectives becomes visible (`contradicts` edge). The reviewer's user yardstick becomes a perspective filter. `global` dissolves by topic, like `workspace` and `subagent.*`: AI-work practice and the user's interaction style go to ~/workspace/ai-architecture, records about a project go to it, and machine and tooling facts go to a small environment area (e.g. ~/workspace/environment). There is no personal area.
Why: The collections mixed two axes. `subagent.the-coder` used the party as a location, so 179 project-specific records sat outside their projects. `user` is a kind although it is a party. `global` was the location for 'topic unknown'. Keeping the party inside the record lets the librarian deliver both perspectives on one question (user's idea, 2026-10-10). That mirrors the evidence/inference split the user applies to sources: who claims something belongs to the claim.
Scope: docs/adr-format.md (optional `perspective:`), navigation reference, archivist (sets perspective), librarian (answers by perspective), chunks 1, 2, 5. Open for the planner: whether the `user` kind folds into `perspective: user` or stays as a kind.

Decision: /reflect at a context boundary produces two things. (1) A carry-only-conclusions handoff: charter, conclusions, open points, no history. This is state and updates FOCUS.md or a docs/handoff-<date>.md. (2) Record candidates for the archivist: decisions and learnings. The next session's charter or briefing is the question to the librarian. So every boundary has a read side (librarian) and a write side (archivist). The orchestrator runs /reflect for the overview, and subagents deliver candidates in their [retro] block.
Why: A context boundary is where the situation is explicit (an earlier record (id withheld)). Troy's handoff is the trigger for writing that ai-mem lacked. Separating handoff from records keeps state and decisions apart (an earlier record (id withheld)).
Scope: /reflect (skills/examples/reflect.md), handoff protocol skill, setup assistant (finds a team's boundaries), chunks 2 and 4 of docs/target_picture_plugin.md.

Decision: Records distinguish three kinds of knowledge that age differently. State (FOCUS.md, handoffs) is overwritten. Decisions with their reasons (records) are only added to, and outdated ones are superseded, not deleted. Evidence (docs/sources/<slug>.md, raw material such as transcripts in docs/sources/<slug>/) stays unchanged. The name and place were agreed on 2026-10-10. The sources/ and transcripts/ folders in interview-notes and the SAG area arose ad hoc and move there. The archivist never edits evidence. A learning that rests on a source points to it (Evidence: path, or derived_from when the source is a record).
Why: Mixing them lets state overwrite reasons, or lets interpretation creep into evidence. Separating what a source says from what we infer keeps claims checkable, which is the user's epistemic working style (an earlier record (id withheld) in ~/workspace/interview-notes; ai-architecture handoff, conclusion 1).
Scope: Navigation reference, archivist rules, adr-format.md (evidence as a recognised layer next to docs/records/ and docs/reference/), docs/target_picture_plugin.md.

Decision: The why of a task reaches the coder through the handoff. /chunk-plan already asks the librarian. It writes the decisions relevant to each chunk into the chunk spec, as id plus one line of why (carry-only-conclusions). At the start of a chunk, the coder asks the librarian only for what the spec does not carry: experience with exactly the files, libraries or tools the chunk touches, from any perspective, with the-coder's own first.
Why: Knowing why a rule exists lets one apply it to cases it did not foresee, and stops one from removing a fence whose purpose is unknown (Chesterton's fence). This holds for humans (user, 2026-10-10) and, as far as known, for models: Anthropic's prompting guidance recommends giving the reason behind an instruction. The planner sees the whole task, the coder the concrete files. Passing the why in the spec costs no extra spawn and keeps nesting flat. This answers the 'coding' trigger point of todo_pull_trigger_points_per_situation.
Scope: chunk-plan.md (spec carries decision ids + why), the-coder.md / dev-team.md coder template (chunk-start librarian call), handoff protocol, chunk 4 of docs/target_picture_plugin.md.

Observed: Chelsea Troy's practices (DDD Europe 2026, distilled in ~/workspace/interview-notes/docs/records/practices/) put a handoff at every context boundary, and what stays of it becomes a record. Each new conversation starts with a charter (scope, terminology, mode). In ai-mem the pull gap test showed that agents read memory only at a fixed trigger, and the review handoff in dev-team.md is such a trigger. Together: a context boundary is both the point to read (the charter or briefing coming in is the question for the librarian) and the point to write (the handoff going out feeds the archivist).
Cause: At a boundary the situation is stated explicitly (charter, diff, chunk spec). Mid-conversation it is implicit, and nothing prompts a read or a write.
Evidence: an earlier record (id withheld) and an earlier record (id withheld) (interview-notes), an earlier record (id withheld), an earlier record (id withheld). A cross-collection edge is not possible yet.

Observed: On 2026-10-10 three areas (~/workspace/ai-architecture, ~/workspace/interview-notes, ~/workspace/ai-architecture/software-architecture-gathering) wrote records by hand, without ai-mem tools. They follow docs/adr-format.md only loosely: Markdown headings and bold labels in the body, an INDEX.md with Markdown links written by hand, no reindex. Two of the areas are not git repos (ai-architecture; interview-notes has `git init` pending). Their READMEs say the archivist will adopt them later.
Cause: Sessions in a fresh area write records the moment insight arises, with nothing at hand but Write. The format stays readable to humans and to the librarian, but drifts from what the tooling generates.
Evidence: ~/workspace/ai-architecture/docs/records/, ~/workspace/interview-notes/docs/records/, software-architecture-gathering/docs/records/README.md.

Observed: The starting question on 2026-10-10 was how ai-mem could give the agent something like experience: knowledge that situational context triggers, the way it does in a living being. An agent has no cheap recognition signal. Pushed content (ranker, autoinject) fired without regard to the situation. What works is pull at fixed points by a role with judgment. Organisations have no recognition either. They keep memory through rituals at boundaries (ADR reviews, handoffs, retros), which is what DDD context maps and Team Topologies describe. ~/workspace/ai-architecture already frames the user's AI work in those terms.
Cause: Interpretation, not measurement. Recognition is not available to the agent, so the working analogue is institutional memory: roles, handoff artifacts and a published format, not a simulated personal memory.
Evidence: this session (2026-10-10), an earlier record (id withheld), ~/workspace/ai-architecture/docs/handoff-2026-10-10.md (conclusion 3).

Observed: In the session of 2026-10-10 the orchestrator did not consult memory when the user's first message set the context (ai-mem, experience on demand, librarian). A rule for exactly that moment existed in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: 'On session start for feature work, query ai-mem ... before planning.'
Cause: The trigger named a category ('feature work'), and that required classifying the session first. A conceptual conversation about ai-mem did not feel like feature work, so the rule did not fire. A trigger works when it names an observable moment ('the first message sets the scope'), not a category.
Evidence: this session; ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, Memory & Context section, rewritten on 2026-10-10 to an observable trigger.

Decision: The librarian is wired in at fixed transition points of the dev team instead of being called situationally by agents. In /dev-team the reviewer asks it at the transition code → review, with the changed paths, against decisions/learnings (in addition to /chunk-plan as the preventive point). The reviewer also reports record_candidates; the reflect gate takes them as the first source for new records, before the coder's learned:.
Why: An agent has no cheap recognition ('I know this') and only asks when an id is already in its context (an earlier record (id withheld)). Ranker and auto-inject fired without relation to the situation. At transitions the context is fresh and concrete (at review: a diff), so the role fixes the situation instead of a hunch. The reviewer has distance from the implementation and can better judge what a record is worth.
Scope: ~/.claude/commands/dev-team.md (reviewer template, [retro] block, reflect gate). Measure: records_consulted. If it stays 'none' over many chunks, the step is ritual and must be reviewed. Open: whether a reviewer spawn can still start an agent (third level); as a fallback the coder asks before the reviewer spawn.
